items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Gay Jones, the paleface, has been doing the sweet work

ctx.x: This was November 8, 1941, Billboard, and it says: Reviewed at the

Rainbow Ballroom, Denver, Ernie Fields. Fields' engagement here was the first for a colored combination, other than for one-nighters and his week showing was one of the best the ballroom has had in several years. Music (inaudible) in that Fields kept on the swing side as well as the usual boogie. Library is extensive enough to cover both. Rene Hall takes care of the boogie arrangements while Gay Jones, the paleface, has been doing the sweet work. Regular instrumentation is four reeds, five brass, split three…

that type of tune. Vocal department is handled by Stella Edmonson--Estelle Edmonson--and Melvin Moore. Both are good soloists, former doing jive work while Moore works with the ballads. Different from the good many colored fronters, Fields works for the crowd, using a goodly amount of (inaudible).
